objective: Deliver Vexel as a complete, high-quality Rust vector drawing and 2D cartoon animation application for Apple Silicon macOS 13+, fully implemented, integrated, comprehensively tested, packaged, documented, and ready for real use. Port every first-party application, platform, UI, XML/SVG parser/rasterizer, geometry, scene, document, project, animation, MCP, development, test, benchmark, and release component to Rust while preserving migration references and frozen acceptance evidence. Provide an original modern custom interface informed by Blender and other modern drawing/animation tools; complete vector editing and cartoon animation workflows; faithful source-preserving Inkscape SVG import/export; versioned native projects containing artwork, animation, assets, metadata, and recovery; and measured high performance on large files, including memory, build time, and release bundle size. Provide detailed discoverable, authorized, live and visible MCP control for Codex, Claude Code, and compatible agents, including drawing, editing, animation, undo/redo, save/export, progress, errors, and cancellation. After feature completion, pass comprehensive UI/end-to-end, fidelity, performance, accessibility, malformed-input, recovery, MCP interoperability, and packaged fresh-install acceptance, fix release blockers, and deliver release artifacts and documentation. Record authentic Codex prompts creating a character, revising the drawing, animating it, and revising that animation through successive real MCP calls while the same Vexel project visibly updates live, with reusable projects, prompts, exports, captions/transcript, and accepted website/README presentation. Preserve macOS-only initial support, MPL-2.0, owned SVG/XML/raster code, minimal audited pinned dependencies, no GPL editor source or external SVG fetching, and safe ownership/resource limits. Use useful disjoint parallel Luna Codex exec workers at task-appropriate effort and Standard speed within the existing subscription allowance, with named escalations only; keep focused correctness checks during implementation and reserve broad automated UI/E2E for the final stage. Completion requires all agreed product outcomes and release evidence, not foundation tests or partial functionality.

tracker.stored_objective: Deliver the owner-approved Vexel product: a high-quality macOS-first vector drawing and 2D animation application with a modern task-focused UI, faithful Inkscape SVG import/export and preservation, a versioned native project format for artwork/animation/assets, high performance on large documents, and live, observable, user-controlled MCP operation for Claude Code, Codex, and compatible agents. Update the governing product decision and roadmap, then implement the remaining capability in scoped repository work orders; reserve the comprehensive UI/end-to-end acceptance pass for the end while retaining focused correctness checks during implementation.
tracker.scope_supplement: canonical full Rust objective and complete outcome/finish-line contract

definition_of_done.title: Full scope delivered.
definition_of_done.requirements:
All nine deliverable areas and agreed feature
   coverage are implemented and integrated. The migration inventory is closed;
   application and first-party tooling use Rust. Required production workflows
   contain no unfinished placeholders or mock backends.

definition_of_done.title: Complete user workflows work.
definition_of_done.requirements:
A user can launch, create/edit vector art,
   import supported Inkscape SVG, animate a character, undo/redo, save/reopen
   projects with assets and animation intact, recover work and export results.
   Actual Codex and Claude Code sessions drive the live app visibly and safely.

definition_of_done.title: Comprehensive final testing passes.
definition_of_done.requirements:
After feature completion, run the
   supported unit/integration/regression checks and full automated UI/E2E pass,
   SVG fidelity/source-preservation corpus, malformed-input/property/fuzz checks
   where specified, project compatibility/recovery, animation appearance/timing,
   MCP interoperability/permissions/progress/cancellation and release checks.
   Record coverage and actual results; skipped or blocked required checks cannot
   count as passes. Preserve frozen assertions and oracles.

definition_of_done.title: Product quality is accepted.
definition_of_done.requirements:
Measured large-file responsiveness and
   memory budgets pass on named hardware. Keyboard/accessibility/display-scale
   and representative-user reviews pass. Fix and rerun affected checks for all
   release-blocking findings, including crashes, corruption/data loss, broken
   required workflows, permission failures and unmet acceptance gates. Document
   remaining nonblocking limitations with evidence; do not claim zero possible
   defects or unlimited SVG compatibility.

definition_of_done.title: The packaged product is usable.
definition_of_done.requirements:
Verify the intended release artifact on
   a clean installation/profile for supported macOS: install, launch, open/save,
   animate/export and connect the supported MCP clients without a developer
   checkout. Validate required platform permissions and distribution behavior
   for the chosen release channel. Deliver versioned artifacts, installation/
   getting-started guidance, supported-feature/format documentation, live-agent
   setup instructions, example projects and release notes.

definition_of_done.title: Showcase delivered.
definition_of_done.requirements:
Review an authentic live Codex recording covering
   character creation, drawing revision, animation creation and animation
   revision through successive MCP calls, with the same Vexel project visibly
   updating. Include playback, save/reopen, exported animation, accessible
   captions/transcript and reusable project/prompts/exports; publish/link the
   accepted video through both website and README.

definition_of_done.title: Final evidence reconciled.
definition_of_done.requirements:
Complete release requirements/coverage matrix,
   accepted work orders, inventory, test/performance results, documented
   limitations and release checklist agree with the shipped version. Completion
   is declared only against that evidence, never from plans, worker exits,
   foundation tests or partially usable functionality.

execution_policy.models: Luna by default at task-appropriate effort; named Sol/Astra escalation only when it reduces rework
execution_policy.parallelism: useful disjoint Codex exec workers; one writer per module; coordinator owns shared contracts/manifests/integration
execution_policy.billing: existing subscription allowance only; no purchased credits or API billing
execution_policy.broad_ui_e2e: after feature completion, then fix findings and rerun release acceptance

completion_requires: every agreed deliverable and final evidence gate; skipped/blocked required checks are not passes
supplements: WO-RUST-GOAL-06 clarifies live iterative demo acceptance; WO-RUST-GOAL-05 remains preserved historical evidence.

sequence: Prompt to draw a specific character
Follow-up prompt to revise the drawing
Prompt to animate that character and show playback
Follow-up prompt to revise animation and show updated timeline/playback
Save/reopen native project and show exported animation
live_demo_acceptance.live_evidence: Real conversation and same live Vexel project visible together; progressive application changes through successive actual MCP calls; retain original footage and privacy-reviewed execution evidence; label cuts/speed changes.
